clue.text: Nasty attitude shown by vermin chasing old woman

indicators.note: the vermin chase, so they come after, the old woman

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for one's mother, an old woman in slang
lice are parasitic insects, classic vermin

explanation.surface: Someone's nasty attitude shows when pests are seen pursuing an elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or ill will is a nasty attitude towards others, the sense of the word here.

clue.text: The writer is supported by a home of the least ostentation

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, so is held up by, what follows

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: The author lives in the plainest, least showy house.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer a piece 'supported by' another stands on top of it, so ME comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of mean in its sense of shabby or humble describes the least ostentatious thing.

clue.text: Clear criminal will have understanding of theft

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of the word clear are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: nous is common sense or understanding

explanation.surface: A plainly guilty person who is clever enough to understand stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an adjective but it is the anagram fodder, and 'criminal' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, so the adjective describes anything relating to stealing.

clue.text: Scottish writer, source of comment that's really outrageous

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter
outrageous signals the letters of really are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish author is quoted as the origin of a shocking remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges the word 'really' to give the letters after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a nineteenth-century Scottish historian and essayist, a famous man of letters.

clue.text: Was made Duke, keeping leader of Lords fixed to the spot?

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, here the leader of Lords

parts.note: became means was made into something

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone was ennobled as a duke while holding a seat in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: a sailing ship left without wind cannot move.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship without wind stays motionless, held in place on the water as if stuck.

clue.text: Gently shifted how many verbs take the past tense?

definitions.meaning: moved carefully and slowly into place, as a load is lowered

definitions.text: how many verbs take the past tense?
definitions.meaning: a verb ending in E, like bake or love, forms its past by turning that final E into ED

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the letters as 'E as ED': a verb ending in E makes its past tense by turning that E into ED. The blogger offered this parse, with some doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To move something slowly and carefully, easing it into position, is to shift it gently.

clue.text: Masterful opening of mine will bring in a couple of Royalty

indicators.note: the mine opening takes in letters, holding them inside

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

indicators.note: a couple of letters means the first two of the word

explanation.surface: A skilful mine entrance will attract a pair of royals.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a mining term for a level entrance tunnel, a word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilful and dexterous handles things in a masterly way.

clue.text: Covering area around tip of Long Island

indicators.note: the covering and area go around the tip of Long

parts.note: a mat is a floor covering

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A surface layer encircling the far end of Long Island in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long Island' looks like one place, but Long gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean nation south of Sicily is an island state.

clue.text: Was rude about accepting uniform no longer current

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside

parts.note: to diss someone is to be rude about them
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone mocked an outdated school uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in use or in service is no longer current.

clue.text: Part of Europe raised assistance to contain upheaval in 7

indicators.note: the reversed help holds the jumbled island inside
in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aid means assistance

indicators.note: an upheaval throws the letters of the island into disorder

parts.note: 7 refers to the answer of 7 down, the island

explanation.surface: A region of Europe lifts aid to deal with turmoil on a cross-referenced island.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the 7-down answer; 'upheaval in' jumbles it, and 'raised' turns the word for help upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic region on the Croatian Adriatic coast is a part of Europe.

clue.text: Atmospheric phenomenon damaging as to USA rural air

indicators.note: damaging suggests the letters of the phrase are broken up and re-formed

explanation.surface: Something in the atmosphere is harming the air of rural America.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern lights are a glowing display in the upper atmosphere caused by solar particles.

clue.text: Some military men evidently will force us back?

definitions.text: Some military men evidently will force us back?

indicators.note: back tells us the hidden letters are read from right to left
some means only part of the words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Soldiers seem set to drive us into retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The run YMENE sits inside 'military men evidently'; 'back' reverses it. The whole clue also describes hostile troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing troops in war are the foe, who would try to push us into retreat.

clue.text: Songs from The King and I having crazy women about

indicators.note: the crazy women go about, around, the king and I

parts.note: mad means crazy
gals is informal for women
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Tunes from the musical The King and I feature a pack of wild women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' looks like the musical's title, but gives R and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied part-songs of the Renaissance for several voices are a kind of song.

clue.text: What's dished up in basket? Note, not chicken!

definitions.text: What's dished up in basket? Note, not chicken!

indicators.note: dished up suggests the letters are served up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Diners expecting chicken in a basket are told to expect something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished up' rearranges BASKET NOTE. 'Chicken in a basket' is a classic British pub meal; the whole clue describes a different dish served.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef with a bone shaped like a letter is a meat dish, not poultry.

clue.text: Upland volcano rising in adjacent space

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a moor is an area of open upland
Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: A volcano erupts on high moorland next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses MOORETNA as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A small waiting room leading into a larger one is a space next to it.

clue.text: Mostly exclude turning out?

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned round, read backwards
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: to debar is to exclude or ban

explanation.surface: A question about largely shutting someone out by expulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts DEBAR to DEBA; 'turning' reverses it. 'out' here means asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tucked up in bed is out for the count, asleep.

clue.text: Drink suppliers were realigned, investing in cheese products

indicators.note: investing in means going inside, here inside the cheeses

parts.note: bries are soft French cheeses

indicators.note: realigned means the letters of were are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Beverage firms have repositioned themselves, putting money into the cheese business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'realigned' rearranges the clue's 'were' into a jug word, which then sits inside the cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies that make beer supply drink to pubs and shops.

clue.text: Band to go without opening in London

indicators.note: without means the following letter is removed

parts.note: in British slang to go to the toilet is to have a slash

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musical group is told to set off without a gig in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' here is British slang for urinating, which is also 'slash'; dropping the L of London leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long strip of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist is a band of fabric.

clue.text: They pass round writing accessories after writer's departed

indicators.note: departed means the writer's piece has gone, removed

parts.note: pencil sharpeners are accessories for writing
a pen is a writer's tool

explanation.surface: People hand around stationery once the author has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departed' removes PEN from SHARPENERS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who split things with others hand portions around among the group.

clue.text: Ravers dancing in sporty gear

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: Clubbers bop about wearing athletic clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravers are people who go to wild parties, revellers out for a good time.

clue.text: Game company bringing in one very much in cheerful style

indicators.note: bringing in means taking a letter inside

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game
I is the Roman numeral for one
so means very much, as in so tired

explanation.surface: A games company takes on someone very jolly.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is a Japanese strategy board game; the musical term is Italian for playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction tells performers to play playfully and merrily.

clue.text: Shiver? That's trembling, with little hesitation

indicators.note: trembling means the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone shudders and trembles, stammering slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' rearranges THAT'S into SHATT. 'Shiver' as a verb also means smash to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver something is to break it into splinters, as in shiver my timbers.

clue.text: Dash quickly, losing time, with spies in pursuit

indicators.note: in pursuit means coming after, so placed behind
losing means a letter is taken away

parts.note: fast means quickly
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off at speed while secret agents chase them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb but is short for dashboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard of a car is also called by this name, the panel facing the driver.

clue.text: One assesses amount of interest about a positive review

indicators.note: about means going around something

parts.note: APR is the annual percentage rate, the interest charged on a loan
praise is a favourable review

explanation.surface: Someone evaluates a loan's interest and gives it a favourable write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word here; APR is the annual percentage rate quoted on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuer who sets the worth of property or goods is someone who assesses.

clue.text: Feature of organ putting depth amongst sound of bells

indicators.note: amongst means placed in the middle of

parts.note: a peal is the ringing sound of bells

explanation.surface: A church organ's design adds depth to the ringing bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Organs have a keyboard played by the feet, whose foot-operated keys belong to the instrument.

clue.text: Irish county making most of remote opportunity

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: a slim chance is a remote one
a go is a chance or opportunity

explanation.surface: A county in Ireland seizing a faint chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland takes its name from its town.

clue.text: Theatrical company engaged in a Ring recalled — as experts in this?

definitions.text: Theatrical company engaged in a Ring recalled — as experts in this?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, read backwards
engaged in means placed inside

parts.note: a ring is round, so O
rep is short for repertory theatre company

explanation.surface: Actors are booked for a revival of Wagner's Ring cycle, as specialists would be.
explanation.walkthrough: REP goes inside A and O to make AREPO; 'recalled' reverses it. Wagner's Ring is the classic example of the art form.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle is a set of staged musical dramas, the art form specialists would know.

clue.text: Medical expert in lesion doctoring, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may be rearranged to give another word

explanation.surface: A specialist is involved in treating a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctoring' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'possibly' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in hormones and glands is a kind of medical doctor.

clue.text: Name of artist very into greens and gold

indicators.note: into here means the very abbreviation is pushed inside the greens dish

parts.note: a salad is a dish of greens
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A painter who is very keen on vegetables and wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter, so this is an artist's first name.

clue.text: Person going to medico for cat?

indicators.note: going to means joining on after

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a user is a person who uses something, such as a service

explanation.surface: Who's the patient visiting the doctor on behalf of the cat?
explanation.definitionFit: A cat that catches rodents is a hunter of mice, often kept on farms.
